pages.title: Forward Itô SDE well-posedness
requirements: Use the existing canonical P-SDE-01 page slug, but complete only the strong-solution slice required by BCS-55. Define d-dimensional Ito SDE with finite-coordinate matrix integrals, strong solution, pathwise uniqueness and global solution on a finite horizon.

On a complete usual filtered space supporting filtration-relative m-dimensional Brownian motion, take F_0-measurable X_0 in L2 with independence of future increments; coefficients jointly Borel in time/state, uniformly globally Lipschitz in state and of uniform linear growth. Prove adapted continuous strong existence and indistinguishable pathwise uniqueness by Picard iteration, scalar Ito isometry/maximal estimates summed over coordinates and Gronwall. Provide finite-horizon E sup |X_t|^2 bound with constants independent of later numerical mesh.

Carry the existing AC/filtration hypotheses wherever consumed. Make integrand predictability/progressive measurability and continuous versions explicit. Prove required moment estimates and any completeness/limit/interchange step locally or cite an exact existing proved interface.

For higher-moment numerical consumers, provide exact-solution finite-p moment estimates under X_0 in Lp and global Lipschitz/linear growth for the required p; preserve the separate all-moment specialization. Any additional maximal estimate needed for these higher moments must be proved locally, not assumed from the L2 bound.

Do not assert positive smooth transition densities, forward-KFP uniqueness, augmented joint KFP regularity or reversal from well-posedness. The broader original ML P-SDE-01 density branch remains a separate unauthored/source-audit obligation, preserved verbatim in this proposal.

pairs.original_provider_clause:
### P-SDE-01 — Forward Itô SDE well-posedness and density regularity

**Pages:** forward-ito-sde-well-posedness / forward-ito-sde-well-posedness-examples. **Scope:** Define an Itô SDE $dX_t=b(t,X_t)dt+\sigma(t,X_t)dW_t$, strong solution, transition density, and forward Kolmogorov equation, with $a=\sigma\sigma^\top$. Separate (i) global strong existence/uniqueness on a complete filtered probability space under Borel time dependence, uniform global Lipschitz-in-state and linear-growth bounds, square-integrable $X_{t_0}$ measurable at $t_0$, and independence of future Brownian increments, from (ii) density regularity: state a separately sourced smoothness/uniform-ellipticity/domain/initial-density theorem that gives a strictly positive smooth $p_t$ and a unique smooth forward Fokker–Planck solution on the stated interval. Anderson also assumes the density of the augmented pair $(X_t,\widetilde W_t)$ and its conditional transition density solve their joint KFP equations uniquely and smoothly; this is a further premise, not a consequence of strong well-posedness. If $X_{t_0}$ may be singular, formulate density and reverse-drift assertions first on $[t_0+\epsilon,T]$; extension to the initial endpoint requires a separately proved limit. **Proof route:** Picard iteration in mean square, coefficient bounds and Grönwall for (i); for (ii), use a named parabolic regularity/heat-kernel theorem with all coefficient, ellipticity, domain, boundary, and initial-data hypotheses matched exactly. Do not infer density smoothness or strict positivity from forward existence. **Examples:** globally Lipschitz scalar drift with nondegenerate constant diffusion; a singular initial law illustrating why smoothness at the initial endpoint is separate. **Requires:** def-d-dimensional-brownian-motion; coordinatewise construction from def-ito-integral-for-square-integrable-predictable-processes and thm-ito-isometry-and-linearity-in-predictable-l2; thm-multidimensional-ito-formula-for-brownian-driven-processes; a strong-solution linear-growth estimate; and a precisely matching PDE density theorem. Vector/matrix Itô integrals must be defined as finite coordinate sums from the existing scalar interface or supplied explicitly. **Sources:** Anderson §§1–4, PDF pp. 1–9, assumes rather than proves forward existence/density regularity and joint-KFP smoothness; Song et al. §§2–4 and appendices pp. 2–5, 13–19, 31–32 use those assumptions. The general density supplier remains open and must be source-audited; this pair precedes P-SDE-02 and any Category 3 consumer.

pages.title: Euler–Maruyama scheme and coefficient conditions
requirements: Define grid t_k=kh on [0,T] with T/h integral, eta_h(t)=max{t_k:t_k<=t}, Euler recursion Y_{k+1}=Y_k+b(t_k,Y_k)h+sigma(t_k,Y_k)(W_{t_{k+1}}-W_{t_k}), step process barY_t=Y_{eta_h(t)}, and continuous interpolation Y_t=X_0+integral_0^t b(eta_h(s),barY_s)ds+integral_0^t sigma(eta_h(s),barY_s)dW_s. State endpoint convention.

State shared exact/numerical assumptions: adapted X_0 in L2 independent of future Brownian increments, Borel coefficients, uniform global state Lipschitz and linear-growth bounds, and |b(t,x)-b(s,x)|+||sigma(t,x)-sigma(s,x)||_F <= K(1+|x|)|t-s|^(1/2). Retain finite horizon and dimension/norm conventions.

Prove adaptedness, well-definedness, grid/continuous/step finite-second-moment estimates uniformly over 0<h<=1, and interpolation increment E|Y_t-barY_t|^2 <= C h. Separate which estimates require time regularity.

Supply uniform finite-p moment bounds needed for weak p>=2q+8 and the all-moment specialization under the corresponding X_0 moment assumptions; do not infer all moments from L2. Do not assert density regularity from the scheme.

pairs.original_provider_clause:
### P-NUM-SDE-01 — Euler–Maruyama scheme and coefficient conditions

**Pages:** euler-maruyama-scheme-and-conditions / euler-maruyama-scheme-and-conditions-examples. **Scope:** Define the Euler–Maruyama recursion $X_{k+1}=X_k+b(t_k,X_k)h+\sigma(t_k,X_k)\Delta W_k$ and its continuous interpolation for $dX_t=b(t,X_t)dt+\sigma(t,X_t)dW_t$. For the later strong theorem, require adapted $X_0$ independent of Brownian increments, $E|X_0|^2<\infty$, Borel time dependence, uniform global Lipschitz and linear-growth bounds in state, and a stated $1/2$-Hölder time modulus with linear growth. Derive finite second moments on $[0,T]$; do not assert density regularity from the scheme. **Proof route:** construct the grid recursion and interpolation; use conditional Brownian moments, Itô isometry, coefficient bounds and Grönwall for moment bounds. **Examples:** scalar additive-noise SDE; superlinear coefficient outside the global-Lipschitz theorem. **Requires:** existing Brownian motion, adapted filtration, predictable Itô integral and isometry; P-SDE-01’s strong solution contract. **Sources:** Song et al. §§2–4, PDF pp. 2–5 and sampling pages 17–19, do not prove this numerical prerequisite. Read a matching numerical-SDE theorem before claiming this result; this pair precedes P-NUM-SDE-02.

pages.title: Euler–Maruyama strong and weak convergence
requirements: Prove a separate finite-L2 theorem under P-NUM-SDE-01 state bounds and half-Holder time modulus: E sup_{t<=T}|X_t-Y_t|^2 <= C h. Use interpolation-defect decomposition, Ito isometry, existing p=2 Ito maximal estimate (the needed BDG specialization) and Gronwall. Constant may depend on T, coefficient constants, dimensions and E|X_0|^2, but not h. This is not a consequence of the H-M-S all-moment theorem.

Preserve a separate autonomous Higham–Mao–Stuart rate theorem with exact C1 drift/diffusion, one-sided Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift, and uniform finite moments of every order for exact, step and continuous Euler processes: E sup_{t<=T}|X_t-Y_t|^2=O(h). Reproduce the full necessary proof locally under the exact source premises; no active unproved import. Derive the globally Lipschitz all-moment specialization only from all-moment X_0. Do not extend the source theorem to nonautonomous coefficients without a separate proof.

Prove conditional weak order one for the chosen bounded test phi: u(t,x)=E phi(X_T^{t,x}) solves backward Kolmogorov, belongs to C^(2,4), with stated time derivatives through two and spatial derivatives through four bounded by C(1+|x|^q), and exact/Euler processes have uniform moments of order p>=2q+8. Specify any mixed derivative control actually used by the Taylor proof rather than assuming it follows without proof. Derive one-step cancellation and expected remainder O(h^2)(1+|x|^(q+4)), then telescope to |E phi(X_T)-E phi(Y_N)|<=C h. Deriving u-regularity merely from coefficient/test smoothness remains an additional independent obligation; this theorem assumes the exact backward regularity.

Define coarse/fine coupling by summing the same fine Brownian increments to form each coarse increment, refinement integer M>=2. Deduce E|Y_T^{h_l}-Y_T^{h_{l-1}}|^2=O(h_l) by the common exact solution and L2 triangle inequality. For globally Lipschitz payoff deduce correction variance O(h_l) and bias O(h_l^(1/2)); under the additional weak contract and Lipschitz payoff deduce bias O(h_l). State per-path work O(h_l^(-1)) under fixed-dimensional unit-cost coefficient/payoff evaluations.

Export rate interfaces to BCS-55 without importing BCS-55 or ML-60. Preserve (alpha,beta)=(1/2,1) and (1,1) with their distinct premises. Learned drift/score bias is outside the solver theorem and requires its own bound.

pairs.original_provider_clause:
### P-NUM-SDE-02 — Euler–Maruyama strong and weak convergence

**Pages:** euler-maruyama-convergence / euler-maruyama-convergence-examples. **Scope:** For the strong rate, state Higham–Mao–Stuart’s exact sufficient contract: $C^1$ drift and diffusion, one-sided Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift, and uniform finite moments of every order for the exact solution, step process, and continuous Euler–Maruyama interpolation on $[0,T]$. Under these hypotheses, $E\sup_{t\le T}|X(t)-Y(t)|^2=O(h)$, so the grid-point RMS error is $O(h^{1/2})$. A global-Lipschitz/linear-growth specialization may derive these moment premises from an initial condition with all finite moments. Do not state only $X_0\in L^2$ as sufficient for this source theorem. For weak order $1$, state the local theorem through backward Kolmogorov regularity: for the chosen bounded test function $\varphi$, require $u(t,x)=E[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})]$ to solve the backward equation and belong to $C^{2,4}$ with its time derivatives through order two and space derivatives through order four bounded by $C(1+\|x\|^q)$. As a conservative explicit sufficient moment condition for the Taylor remainder and telescoping argument, assume the exact and Euler processes have uniform moments of some order $p\ge 2q+8$ on $[0,T]$, obtained from a finite $p$th moment of $X_0$ under globally Lipschitz/linear-growth coefficients. State a sharper exponent only if separately proved. A claim that bounded $C^4$ coefficients and test function imply this $u$-regularity needs its own stochastic-flow/Kolmogorov regularity proof. For fixed $T$ and $0<h\le1$ with $T/h$ integral, Taylor-expand one Euler step in $t$ and the Gaussian state increment through cubic order; the conditional expectation of the cubic Gaussian term vanishes and the fourth-order remainder is $O(h^2)(1+\|x\|^{q+4})$, while $(\partial_t+L_t)u=0$. Telescope over $T/h$ steps and use the stated moment bound to obtain $|E\varphi(X_T)-E\varphi(X_N)|\le Ch$. This weak proof is a local design, not a conclusion certified by the exposition sources. These are solver bounds for the exact SDE only. They do not cover a learned drift/score bias unless that bias is separately bounded and stable. **Proof route:** use Higham–Mao–Stuart’s stopping/localization, moment truncation, interpolation-defect estimate, Itô formula, Burkholder–Davis–Gundy and Grönwall proof for the strong theorem; for the global-Lipschitz specialization, derive moment bounds separately. For weak order, derive the one-step backward-Kolmogorov cancellation and Gaussian Taylor remainder under the stated $C^{2,4}$ polynomial-growth and explicit $p\ge2q+8$ moment hypotheses; cite or prove a separate result deriving this regularity from coefficient assumptions. For coupled MLMC levels, use shared coarse/fine Brownian increments; a globally Lipschitz payoff then has correction variance $O(h)$ and cost $O(h^{-1})$ per sample, giving the BCS-55 conditional Euler example with $(\alpha,\beta)=(1/2,1)$. If the stronger weak-order bound applies to the payoff, bias exponent $\alpha=1$ is available; do not claim this outside that regime. **Examples:** additive-noise Euler error; a nonzero learned-score bias persisting as $h\to0$. **Requires:** P-NUM-SDE-01 — Euler–Maruyama scheme and coefficient conditions; P-SDE-01 and its exact moment contracts. **Sources:** Higham, Mao, and Stuart, “Strong Convergence of Euler-Type Methods for Nonlinear Stochastic Differential Equations,” §2, Assumption 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 with proof (printed pp. 1042–1046), and §4, Assumptions 3.1/4.1/4.2, Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4 with proof (printed pp. 1054–1056), cached-author copy SHA-256 27d372e331e4c519b0d3b592c230f224c81b4585c21e083f80facd14f39fa0ba. Higham’s “An Algorithmic Introduction to Numerical Simulation of Stochastic Differential Equations,” §4 and §5 (printed pp. 532–538; PDF SHA-256 e02942bc821a5eb63c6b7909aacb87b0e95048f0950e796460878390609566f1), defines strong/weak errors and says Euler–Maruyama has weak order $1$ under “appropriate” conditions, but provides numerical illustrations rather than a matching weak-order theorem/proof. Särkkä and Solin, Applied Stochastic Differential Equations, §8.3 (printed pp. 137–139; PDF SHA-256 279156f8f4382faaa253c27697fcb5ff8d75ace5d940d944553b5f3465ea9435), gives the weak-error definition, Euler scheme, and cites the order-$1$ conclusion under sufficient regularity, but does not supply a full proof; its theorem reference is contextual only. Song et al. pp. 17–19 and 31–32 discuss sampling only. ML-60 — Score SDEs and reverse-time generation consumes this only for sampler-error claims.

consumer_requirements.original_bcs_55_clause:
### BCS-55 — Multilevel Monte Carlo and cost theorem
**Pages:** multilevel-monte-carlo / multilevel-monte-carlo-examples. **Scope:** Define geometrically refined levels $h_l=M^{-l}T$, coupled corrections and telescoping expectation. Require independent level estimators and rates: bias $O(h_L^\alpha)$, $\alpha\ge1/2$; correction variance $O(N_l^{-1}h_l^\beta)$, $\beta>0$; cost $O(N_lh_l^{-1})$. State complexity for MSE $\epsilon^2$: $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ if $\beta>1$, $O(\epsilon^{-2}\log^2(\epsilon^{-1}))$ if $\beta=1$, and $O(\epsilon^{-2-(1-\beta)/\alpha})$ if $\beta<1$. The requested square-integrable Euler–Maruyama case uses independent pre-category designs P-NUM-SDE-01/02. Under P-NUM-SDE-01's globally Lipschitz and linear-growth state bounds, $1/2$-Hölder time modulus, adapted initial condition independent of future Brownian increments, and $X_0\in L^2$, a separate local interpolation-error/Itô-isometry/BDG/Grönwall proof gives $E\sup_{t\le T}|X(t)-X^h(t)|^2=O(h)$. With shared Brownian increments on adjacent levels, the $L^2$ triangle inequality gives $E|X_{h_l}(T)-X_{h_{l-1}}(T)|^2=O(h_l)$; for a globally Lipschitz payoff this gives correction variance $O(h_l)$ and path cost $O(h_l^{-1})$, so $\beta=1$. The strong bound alone gives Lipschitz-payoff bias $O(h_L^{1/2})$, hence $\alpha=1/2$ and complexity $O(\epsilon^{-2}\log^2(\epsilon^{-1}))$. This direct finite-$L^2$ proof is a separate local route and is not inferred from Higham–Mao–Stuart. Their source theorem supports the same rate under its exact autonomous contract: $C^1$ drift/diffusion, one-sided Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift, and uniform moments of every order for the exact solution, step process, and continuous interpolation; the globally Lipschitz/linear-growth specialization obtains these moments from an all-moment initial condition. For weak order one, require the separate P-NUM-SDE-02 bounded-test/backward-Kolmogorov contract: $u(t,x)=E[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})]$ solves the backward equation, lies in $C^{2,4}$ with time derivatives through order two and space derivatives through order four bounded by $C(1+\|x\|^q)$, and exact/Euler processes have uniform moments of order $p\ge2q+8$. The local one-step expected Taylor remainder is $O(h^2)(1+\|x\|^{q+4})$; telescoping gives bias $O(h_L)$, so $\alpha=1$. When this payoff is also Lipschitz, $\beta=1$ remains and the same logarithmic complexity follows. Lipschitz payoff alone does not give weak order one. **Proof route:** Prove the abstract theorem by telescoping, variance allocation $N_l\propto\sqrt{V_l/C_l}$, bias/variance budgeting and geometric sums. For the finite-$L^2$ Euler route, prove the strong interpolation estimate locally from the P-NUM-SDE-01 assumptions with Itô isometry, BDG and Grönwall, then use shared increments for the coupled correction bound. Separately, reproduce or explicitly import H-M-S under its exact autonomous all-moment hypotheses; do not transfer those source hypotheses to the finite-$L^2$ route without proof. For weak order, prove the one-step backward-Kolmogorov cancellation and Gaussian Taylor remainder $O(h^2)(1+\|x\|^{q+4})$ under the stated $C^{2,4}$ growth and $p\ge2q+8$ moment hypotheses; deriving that solution regularity from coefficient/payoff assumptions is a separate obligation. Neither Euler rate is part of the abstract MLMC proof, and adaptive bias stopping remains heuristic. **Examples:** the conditional Lipschitz-payoff Euler case $(\alpha,\beta)=(1/2,1)$; the smoother weak-order-one Euler case $(1,1)$; a discontinuous payoff with $\beta=1/2$ and $\alpha=1$; failure when either rate is absent. **Requires:** BCS-25, BCS-54 and standard IID/moment suppliers for the abstract theorem; P-NUM-SDE-01 — Euler–Maruyama scheme and coefficient/moment setup, and P-NUM-SDE-02 — strong/weak rate contracts, only for the conditional Euler cases. These are independent pre-category designs, not completed library proofs; P-NUM-SDE-02 inherits P-SDE-01's strong-solution contract. No Category 4 supplier is used. **Sources:** Giles (2008), “Multilevel Monte Carlo Path Simulation,” Theorem 3.1 and full proof, *Operations Research* 56(3), 607–617, PDF pp. 1–11. Higham, Mao, and Stuart (2002), Theorem 4.4 with full proof and Assumptions 3.1/4.1/4.2, printed pp. 1054–1056, supports strong-rate claims only under its exact autonomous all-moment hypotheses. The finite-$L^2$ route and P-NUM-SDE-02 backward-Kolmogorov weak-rate proof are explicit local proof obligations/designs; the consulted weak-error expositions do not prove them. Adaptive bias stopping is heuristic.
